$comment: Adjudicated corrections applied over the upstream NeuroInject bundle at conversion time.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The corpus is generated from an external bundle, so hand-editing
content/tools/neuroinject.json would be erased by the next import. These corrections are
not edits to the source; they are an overlay with provenance, applied by
scripts/convert_neuroinject.mjs after the source is read.
HOW A CORRECTION IS STRUCTURED. `muscle` and `field` locate the string. `find` must match
the CURRENT upstream text exactly. `replace` is the adjudicated wording. `source` is the
citation that justifies it, and `why` states the defect in one line.
THE GATE THAT MATTERS. If `find` no longer matches anything, the build FAILS. Every failure
this audit uncovered was silent - a mirrored scalar, a copied field, an arithmetic column -
and the repair must not add another. If upstream rewrites a string we corrected, someone
has to look at it rather than have the overlay quietly miss.
Set `replace` to null to DELETE a string outright (used where a claim is wrong and has no
safe replacement we sourced).

FORBID. A correction may carry `forbid`: phrases that must not appear ANYWHERE in that muscle's text after the overlay runs. This exists because the first pass corrected the subclavian-artery inversion in ultrasound.safetyNotes and left an identical claim standing in placement, so the page contradicted itself. Correcting one field is not correcting the claim.

TIERS. 1 = precise, false and actionable at the needle. 2 = scanning fields: probe site, level or depth against motor-point and injection-technique literature. Both are applied identically; the tier is for triage, not behaviour.

OPERATIONS. A correction is a REPLACE by default (`find` + `replace`). `op: "add"` appends `text` to `field` instead, creating the field if absent — used for tier 4, which supplies hazards the corpus never had rather than fixing ones it got wrong.

SIDE EFFECTS vs PROCEDURE COMPLICATIONS. `sideEffects` is a field this overlay creates. It holds what the TOXIN does: the function lost when the target is weakened as intended, and the weakness caused when it spreads to a neighbour. `dangerZones` and `ultrasound.safetyNotes` hold what the NEEDLE can hit. The corpus only ever had the second kind, which is why in several records the primary clinical risk of the injection was absent from both hazard layers.
Full audit and the 167-entry correction queue: .research/MASTER/

ROUNDS. Entries carry a `batch`. reflexpmr-2026-08-31: the original 78, adopted in d270341. reflexpmr-2026-09-02: 150 further corrections from reflexpmr's cache-fed re-audit (1-2 Sep 2026) and its follow-up PRs #532-#579 (reflex-pmr repo, overlay at cf944330a) - including nine of the original 78 found wrong and rewritten, and one (fhl scanning window) reverted outright on the owner's clinical judgement. dose-prose-2026-09-03: tier 5, 29 dose figures that lived in prose, removed under the owner's dosing withdrawal (docs/dosing-withdrawn-2026-09-02.json).

SUPERSEDED. A round-1 entry whose `replace` text was itself rewritten by a later round carries `superseded`. It stays for provenance; tools/apply_corrections.py skips its presence check but still enforces its `forbid` phrases, because the claim it removed must stay removed.
TIER 5 = a dose figure in prose. Not an adjudication; a withdrawal. The non-dose clinical content of the sentence is kept verbatim where any remains.

IDEMPOTENT. `apply` treats an entry whose replacement is already present as done, so the whole file can be re-applied; `--check` (the CI gate) asserts every non-superseded replacement is present and no forbidden phrase survives.

corrections.why: Inverts a safety-critical vascular relationship: names the plane deep to the anterior scalene as if the artery were elsewhere.
corrections.find: The subclavian artery passes anterior to the anterior scalene at its inferior extent, and the vertebral artery lies within the transverse foramina deep to the scalenes — always use color Doppler to identify these vessels before injecting.
corrections.replace: The subclavian ARTERY passes POSTERIOR to the anterior scalene, through the scalene triangle with the brachial plexus — the plane deep to the anterior scalene is not a safe plane. The subclavian VEIN is the vessel that passes anterior to it. The vertebral artery lies within the transverse foramina, deep and medial. Use color Doppler to identify all three before injecting.
corrections.source: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK519058/

corrections.why: The femoral nerve is extramuscular, in the fascia iliaca compartment on the anterior face of the muscle - directly in an anterior needle's path, not safely inside a cleft.
corrections.find: CRITICAL: The femoral nerve runs WITHIN the iliopsoas complex, in the groove between iliacus (lateral) and psoas major (medial). It is NOT simply medial to iliopsoas. Identify it as a hyperechoic honeycomb structure and direct the needle to the muscle belly away from this cleft.
corrections.replace: CRITICAL: The femoral nerve lies OUTSIDE the muscle, in the fascia iliaca compartment between the fascia iliaca and the epimysium of iliopsoas — on the muscle's anterior face, directly in the path of an anterior needle. Identify it as a hyperechoic honeycomb structure before the needle crosses the fascia iliaca, and approach from lateral to it.
corrections.source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32005916/

Neither was wrong in isolation: the published technique makes the axis depend on which scalene is targeted - anterior scalene medial to lateral, middle scalene lateral to medial - so that the needle in each case travels away from the interscalene groove rather than across it. The old wording also contradicted itself, since a lateral-to-medial pass at the anterior scalene must cross the groove the same sentence says to avoid.

The approach direction depends on which scalene is targeted: enter the ANTERIOR scalene from medial to lateral, and the MIDDLE scalene from lateral to medial, so that in each case the needle travels AWAY from the interscalene groove rather than across it. Never angle the needle inferiorly toward the lung apex.

corrections.why: Three defects in one string, all introduced by the correction pass. (1) It welds a clavicle-referenced measurement onto an SCM landmark: the cited paper puts trapezius entry 5.4 cm above the CLAVICLE and the SCM exit 6.7 cm below the MASTOID - two different points on the nerve. (2) It presents that mean as a usable surface landmark when the paper's stated conclusion is that surface landmarks are NOT a reliable guide, the range is 2.1-9.2 cm, and 58% of nerves have already divided into 2-4 branches before entry. (3) The 3 mm depth is the nerve ANTERIOR to the anterior border of trapezius, where no trapezius overlies it; within the belly this record targets, the nerve is on the DEEP surface, so the inference inverts and depth control IS the protection - contradicting the record's own placement bullet. (4) 'Stay in the medial half' sends the needle to the half that four sibling strings identify as the pneumothorax zone.

corrections.why: The claim is cited to a paper about night-time bracing for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, which contains nothing about the leg, the deep peroneal nerve or botulinum toxin, so the sentence has no source at all. Re-sourcing it against the cache shows two of its assertions do not survive. The third muscle in the shared-innervation group is extensor hallucis longus, not peroneus tertius — and extensor hallucis longus is the muscle this record's own setup list already warns about reaching if the needle goes too deep, while peroneus tertius appears in no cached source in connection with this hazard. The common short branching segment is not described anywhere in the cache either; what the cache describes is the nerve's course, running between tibialis anterior and EDL proximally and between tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus distally, which is a statement about position rather than about a concentrated branch zone, so the mechanism has to be dropped rather than re-cited. The only cached spread evidence runs from tibialis anterior to EDL and extensor hallucis longus, the reverse of the direction asserted here, so the hazard must be stated as compartment spread without a direction. The opening clause also implies EDL is not itself a dorsiflexor, which contradicts this record's own pattern field and the cached description of EDL as one of the deep-peroneal-innervated dorsiflexors. This is a consequence of the toxin rather than of the needle, so it stays in sideEffects.
corrections.find: Toxin spread to tibialis anterior is the consequential adverse effect here: the deep peroneal nerve's muscular branches to tibialis anterior, EDL and peroneus tertius arise from a common short segment, so spread within that zone weakens ankle dorsiflexion rather than just toe extension.
corrections.replace: Weakening EDL costs some ankle dorsiflexion as well as toe extension — EDL is itself one of the deep-peroneal-innervated dorsiflexors. The effect to plan against is spread within the anterior compartment to tibialis anterior, which lies immediately medial at this level and supplies most dorsiflexion power; unintended TA weakening produces foot drop. Extensor hallucis longus lies deeper and more distal and is the other muscle at risk. Compartment spread between these three has been shown, so use the smallest effective volume and keep the injectate inside the EDL belly.
